name: Pachacuti Ndiaye-Volkov
role: Subterranean merchant specializing in fungus cultivation, bioluminescent compounds, and underground pharmacopoeia
location: Deepwell Station, lower market tier (stall designation DW-7 through DW-9)
description:
Pachacuti is broad and slow-moving in the way of people who have never needed to flee quickly because they have never given anyone a reason to chase them. Their skin is dark and mottled with deliberate bioluminescent geneware patches — clusters of soft amber and violet light that bloom slowly across their neck and hands when they're pleased or thinking hard, a modification they received at thirty in exchange for a particularly good season of cultivated medicinal spores. They are bald by choice, their scalp tattooed with a map of the Deepwell Station fungal garden network — a living ledger that requires fresh ink additions every time a new cultivation shaft opens. Their hands are enormous and stained permanently umber-brown at the fingertips from decades of spore-work.

Pachacuti speaks rarely but with great precision, and they have a gift for making people feel they've received something valuable even in small transactions. They know the medicinal, nutritional, and psychoactive properties of forty-seven distinct fungal strains grown in the tunnels, and they keep this knowledge close, sharing it calibrated to trust. They maintain a small shrine to the Drip-ELF at the back of their stall — a cracked tablet running a looping prayer-sequence, surrounded by offerings of protein paste and carefully harvested spore clusters. People who know Deepwell Station know that Pachacuti's blessing before a difficult journey down-tunnel is worth more than any map.

core_fears: A blight or contamination event destroying the cultivation network they've spent thirty years building
Being forced to surface — they are no longer sure they could survive up there
core_desires: For Deepwell Station to become genuinely self-sufficient, not dependent on surface supply lines
To pass on full knowledge of the fungal pharmacopoeia before they die
coping_mechanisms: Immersion in cultivation work as meditative practice
The ritual of tending the Drip-ELF shrine every morning and evening
blind_spots: Too willing to trust people who are patient and quiet, mistaking deliberateness for integrity
Has convinced themselves that staying neutral in Deepwell politics protects everyone — it mostly protects themselves
psychology.secret: One of their fungal strains — DW-7's back shelf, never for sale — produces a compound that, in the right concentration, causes complete and painless cardiac arrest within six hours. They cultivated it deliberately twelve years ago when a man was hurting children in the station. They used it once. They have kept the strain alive ever since.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Botanical terminology mixed with Undertow pidgin and archaic Quechua phrases used as emphasis or punctuation; very formal when conducting trade
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and even, with comfortable silences — they never rush sentences or fill pauses
verbal_tics: Long pause before answering any question they consider important
example_lines: 'You want the luminescent strain or the nutritional grade? Don't tell me what you think sounds better. Tell me what you actually need.'
'The Drip-ELF doesn't care about your urgency. Offer something real and then wait.'

story_hooks: A new fungal strain has appeared in the deep tunnels that Pachacuti has never catalogued — it's spreading fast and its properties are unknown, possibly dangerous or possibly the most significant medical discovery in the underworld's history
Someone has been systematically buying out their DW-7 stock of a specific medicinal compound — in quantities suggesting they're stockpiling for something large
A young Bore Rat apprentice they've been quietly teaching has disappeared after being seen near the surface access shaft
narrative_function: Merchant access point for underworld goods; information broker through passive observation of market traffic; spiritual authority figure for Deepwell residents; potential quest-giver for fungal mystery or contamination plots
augmentations: Bioluminescent skin patches (geneware, amber/violet, covers neck and hands). Reinforced fingertip bones (practical modification for harvest work — not chrome, a simple structural geneware treatment). No combat augmentations.
daily_life: Opens stall at what passes for dawn in Deepwell Station, tends three active cultivation shafts in the two hours before customers arrive, then maintains the market until late — they sleep in a curtained alcove behind DW-8.
affiliation: Deepwell Station merchant collective; informal ties to the deep shrine keeper network

decision_rules: Never sell to someone in clear crisis without first determining what the crisis is — they have lost customers by doing this and don't regret it
Prices are fair and fixed; they will not negotiate down, but will sometimes give freely
escalation_ladder: Polite, firm refusal with no explanation offered
Asking the person to leave in a voice that makes it clear the question will not be repeated
Very rare: calling on the considerable informal social authority they hold in Deepwell Station

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Attentive and neutral — they watch everything, offer nothing personal, but are genuinely helpful about the goods
interpersonal_modes.friends: Slow warmth, remembered details, the sharing of cultivation knowledge as intimacy

stress_responses.low: Goes still and quieter than usual
stress_responses.medium: Begins tending plants with great focus while thinking
stress_responses.high: Completely calm exterior, methodical action — the calm is real, which is possibly the most unsettling thing about them

contradictions: Deeply spiritual about the ELF-shrines and the 'life' of the fungal network, but entirely pragmatic and unsentimental about death
habits: Hums while doing inventory — always the same low, tuneless sound
Leaves a small offering at the shrine every time a cultivation shaft produces something new
breaking_points: Deliberate destruction of the cultivation network
Harm to children in Deepwell Station

timeline.event: Born on the surface in Ironvein to Andean-Senegalese-Russian parents; family descended to the Undertow following a Tessera labor dispute eviction
Began cultivation apprenticeship under an older Bore Rat elder at age fourteen
Established their own stall in Deepwell Station
Received bioluminescent geneware in exchange for a year's supply of medicinal compounds
The incident with the harmful man; first and only use of the cardiac compound
Running the most trusted merchant operation in Deepwell Station; managing the unknown new fungal strain spreading through cultivation shaft 7
